summary: Merano (Meran) charges for on-street parking through Blue Park zones: under the ordinance, Zone A is paid every day and Zone B Monday to Saturday (08:00-19:00), with a Zone C reserved for tourist coaches; the city's general parking page simplifies this to Monday to Sunday. The municipal executive decided in December 2022 to adjust the hourly rates (2.50 euro in Zone A, 1.50 euro in Zone B) from the start of 2023, and residents without a private space can apply for subscriptions; the sources do not show whether those rates are still current in 2026. The historic centre is a camera-enforced restricted traffic zone with four monitored entry points. The city council approved the mobility plan (PUMS) and traffic plan (PGTU) on 11 March 2025. The big structural change is the 594-space Kavernengarage under the Küchelberg, a public-private project financed by private partners (the investor group Meran Centrum Parking AG) in return for a 50-year concession; in February 2025 it was reported to be due to open together with the Küchelberg tunnel in autumn 2026, but the city's 7 October 2026 release gives no separate garage opening date or price. That release plans the bypass opening ceremony for 21 November and traffic release for 26 November 2026, and first city-centre measures from January 2027, including a reorganisation of central-area parking linked to the new garage; a hospital shuttle is only an idea. The province's planned station mobility centre (about 350 underground commuter spaces in a December 2024 report) now has construction expected in 2028-2029 according to the city. The hospital car park is reported full on school-term weekday mornings, and three Landtag members report heavy use of the Therme Meran garage (347,598 vehicles in a year) and expect lower revenue if traffic really leaves the centre. Live availability of city-centre car parks is said to be on mobility.meran.eu, but that site could not be read.

items.text: The municipal executive (Gemeindeausschuss) unanimously decided on 20 December 2022 to adjust the Blue Park tariffs, taking effect at the start of 2023. The page lists 2.50 euro per hour in Zone A and 1.50 euro in Zone B, and subscriptions of 180 euro (6 months) and 280 euro (12 months) for the first subscription, 270 and 420 euro for the second. The page does not say whether these rates are still current in 2026.
items.source_title: Änderung Parkgebühren Blaue Zonen - Stadtgemeinde Meran

items.text: The municipal Blue Park ordinance divides paid street parking into Zone A (paid every day) and Zone B (paid Monday to Saturday), marked by signs and blue lines. Residents without a private parking space, social institutions and people with disabilities can apply for subscriptions; the street lists are in an annex PDF that was not opened.
items.source_title: Verordnung über die Parkzonen Blue Park - Stadtgemeinde Meran

items.text: As of the page's last update on 7 May 2026, the city says blue-marked street spaces are paid Monday to Sunday from 08:00 to 19:00, with tickets bought at nearby machines or paid by mobile apps (a virtual ticket is issued for the licence plate and only the actual parking time is paid). The city's Blue Park ordinance, however, makes Zone B paid only Monday to Saturday, so the page's blanket statement is simplified. The page points to mobility.meran.eu for locations and free spaces of the large city-centre car parks and links an urban parking concept (Stadtparkraumkonzept).

The city centre has several restricted traffic zones (ZTL) monitored by fully automated cameras at four points: Postbrucke, Obere Freiheitsstrasse/Theaterplatz, Galileistrasse after the Algunder Kellerei car park, and Zenobergstrasse (Passeirer Tor). All Merano taxis and the vehicles of Anrainer (adjacent residents) are on the authorised list, only within permitted times and following the signs, and people with a disability card can apply for a permit. Checks are digital only and fines are issued automatically (page last updated 6 May 2026).
items.source_title: Durchfahrt einer verkehrsbeschränkten Zone - Stadtgemeinde Meran

items.text: The city council approved the sustainable urban mobility plan (PUMS, resolution no. 11) and the general urban traffic plan (PGTU, resolution no. 12) on 11 March 2025. The city page lists the plan documents but does not itself describe parking measures.
items.source_title: Piano urbano della mobilità sostenibile (PUMS) con annesso Piano Generale del Traffico Urbano (PGTU) - Comune di Merano

items.text: The city presented a mobility concept ('Kurstadt 2.0') and plans first city-centre measures from January 2027, including traffic calming, reversed flows in some streets, and a reorganisation of central-area parking linked to the new Kavernengarage. The north-west bypass has an opening ceremony planned for 21 November and traffic release on 26 November 2026; a shuttle bus to the hospital, Rennweg, the thermal baths and Untermais station is only an idea so far.
items.source_title: Kurstadt 2.0: Schritt für Schritt zu neuer Mobilität - Stadtgemeinde Meran

items.text: The city says the hospital car park is full on weekdays during school term, roughly 07:30 to 12:00. A plan for the health area envisages about 700 spaces, 155 more than today.
items.source_title: Kurstadt 2.0: Schritt für Schritt zu neuer Mobilität - Stadtgemeinde Meran

items.text: The Kavernengarage under the Küchelberg is a public-private partnership: the private partners financed it fully in return for a 50-year concession to run the car park. It is planned with 594 spaces, 12 EV charging stations and car-sharing spaces; cost rose from 27 to 39 million euro, and opening is not before 2026 because access depends on the second bypass tunnel section.
items.source_title: Kavernengarage: Ausschuss- und Ratsmitglieder besichtigen die Baustelle - Südtirol News

items.text: When the city reached its agreement with the investor group in 2019, reported terms included a maximum hourly rate of 2.40 euro (adjustable for inflation) and a monthly pass capped at 183 euro. The city was to receive payments for up to 300 on-street blue spaces removed, starting at 150 euro per space per year; the final contract terms were not checked.
items.source_title: Il garage in caverna avrà 600 posti - Alto Adige

items.text: In February 2025 the cavern garage, built by Meran Centrum Parking AG with the municipality, was reported to be due to open at the same time as the Küchelberg tunnel, which was planned for autumn 2026. The municipality had spent about 6 million euro on securing works, against an estimate of 3.7 million two years earlier.

In a written question to the provincial government (dated 10 August 2026), three South Tyrol Landtag members (Madeleine Rohrer, Brigitte Foppa and Zeno Oberkofler) state that 347,598 vehicles parked in the Therme Meran underground garage in the previous year and that parking brought in more than 2.3 million euro, the third-largest revenue item of the baths after pools and sauna and catering. They say revenue is likely to fall once the tunnel and Kavernengarage open, provided motorised traffic is really banned from the city centre. These are the MPs' figures; no reply was found.
items.source_title: Was passiert in Meran nach der Eröffnung des Küchelbergtunnels? (Anfrage, Südtiroler Landtag)

items.text: On the operator's FAQ (undated page, read October 2026), Terme Merano visitors with a day ticket can add 16 euro to park until midnight. With a 2 to 3 hour ticket the first hour is free and each further hour costs 3.20 euro; the 16 euro day option is not available during the whole Advent and Christmas season.
items.source_title: Answers to frequently asked questions - Terme Merano

items.text: On its own undated page (read October 2026), the St. Josef garage advertises 90 public, videomonitored spaces with 2 EV charging stations. It lists 1.40 euro per half hour from 07:00 to 20:00 and 0.90 euro per half hour overnight, open 24 hours.

The city commissioned Neogy (an Alperia and Dolomiti Energia company) to install 18 new charging columns at 11 locations, with the aim of 50 public charge points by 2025. The report lists six public columns with 12 charge points as the starting point, and a planned hub at Bahnhof Untermais with 3 hyperchargers and 3 fast 22 kW chargers.
items.source_title: Elektromobilität in Meran: 18 neue Ladesäulen an elf Standorten - Südtirol News

items.text: On 30 December 2024 the provincial government gave the start signal for planning and building a new mobility centre on the railway station site. The report describes about 350 parking spaces reachable underground, mainly for commuters, about 1,000 covered bike spaces, and a cost of about 28.4 million euro (16.5 million from the national development and cohesion fund, over 11.9 million from the province). The report said planning would start in 2025 and realisation in 2026.
items.source_title: Mobilitätszentrum Meran: Technische Daten und Finanzierung genehmigt - Südtirol News

items.text: Stadtwerke Meran AG, wholly owned by the municipality, lists parking lots and garages in Meran among its responsibilities alongside water, environmental services and public lighting (page last updated 2 October 2025). The page gives no locations, capacities or rates, and does not say which car parks it runs.

gaps: https://www.stol.it/artikel/panorama/meran-keine-tiefgarage-am-theaterplatz - only the headline was readable, no body or date (reported council vote on an underground garage at Theaterplatz not used).

https://www.stol.it/artikel/chronik/kavernengarage-kostet-knapp-6-millionen-mehr - only the headline was readable; the reported Meran Centrum Parking request to raise the hourly tariff from 2.40 to 2.50 euro could not be confirmed from a page I read (the 31 Jul 2024 Südtirol News piece on the 5.9 million euro contribution does not mention it).
https://mobility.meran.eu - the city's live car-park availability site returned no readable content, so the parking guidance system, its car parks and occupancy could not be checked.
The Blue Park ordinance PDF and its street-list annex, and the Stadtparkraumkonzept and the 'Tariffe parcheggi bluepark' pages linked from the city pages, were not opened.
The city's two pages differ on Blue Park hours (Parkplätze page: paid Monday to Sunday 08:00-19:00; ordinance page: Zone B paid Monday to Saturday); not resolved.

https://www.telepass.com/it/privati/servizi/strisce-blu/merano - commercial and undated, not used. Parkhaus Plaza, Karl-Wolf, Meranarena, Obermais and Algunder Kellerei tariffs only appear on undated or 2023 private/tourism pages (e.g. https://www.visitmeran.it/parkplaetze-meran/, 'Update August 2023'), so they are not recorded.

No readable source found for: Etschwerke/SEAB, a 'Meraner Parkhaus-Gesellschaft', SASA's role in parking or park-and-ride, Parkhaus Theatergarage/Kurhaus/Postgebäude/Gärtnerei projects, and any Dolomiten, Rai Südtirol or Alto Adige piece on 2025-2026 parking usage statistics.

No official Gemeinde notice found on parking or traffic measures for the Christkindlmarkt; the organiser page https://www.christkindlmarkt.it/de/anreise-christkindlmarkt-meran is undated and only generic, so it is not recorded.
The final tariff and opening date of the Kavernengarage are not confirmed by any page I read; the city's October 2026 release gives bypass dates but no separate garage opening date or price.
The Landtag question (LTG_0005103) has no reply in the sources found, and the 'Therme Meran' figures are the MPs' own.
